title: The Ten Quiet Turns

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Louder, then. And faster.
directions: [board: a clock in slippers, asleep on a cushion. Pip jogs a lap around it, blowing a small trumpet. The clock does not stir.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Running in circles is exercise. It is not a clock reset.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Then I will try the drum. Quietly. In case it is listening.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: A second thing to count. I have waited nine episodes.
directions: [board: Click is handed a strip of ten spaces. Nine are filled. One is empty.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Click, how many quiet turns have we counted?
directions: [card: QUIET BULLETIN · nine of ten · outlook: quiet]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Nine. Nine finished player turns with no enemy killed by attack.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A quiet turn has no enemy killed by attack. Collecting crystals does not reset this clock.
directions: [card: ONE FINISHED PLAYER TURN FILLS ONE SPACE · not one round · not ten actions]
[card: A QUIET TURN · nobody removed by an attack · no crystals at the end]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ten quiet turns in a row, and the game is a draw.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Four things happened, and one was letting a Hono go. The clock slept through all four.
directions: [board: a practice strip beside the real one. Pip buys a piece and it sleeps. Pip promotes a piece and it sleeps. Pip hits a Sjor, the Sjor is still standing, and it sleeps. Pip cannot pay a Hono's bill and lets the Hono go, and it sleeps.]
[card: DOES NOT WAKE THE CLOCK BY ITSELF · buying · promoting · a hit they survive · letting a piece go at the bill]
lines.performanceNote: Hono is pronounced ho-no, two smooth syllables, with no k sound. Read the exact words.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Dramatic is not the same as busy. I think walking all the way across still counts as quiet.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Walking never resets it. Neither does mining, buying, promoting, or a hit the target survives.
directions: [board: separate White Action practice position. A White Hi walks A five to J five along an open row for five actions and stops on a square with zero reserve. No attack kill this turn; every other White ending square also has zero reserve. End turn: the practice strip gains one space. No automatic fight occurs along the walk.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: That square paid. The quiet clock kept counting.
directions: [sfx: crystal clink] [board: reset that practice position. The same Hi makes the same walk; J five now holds one crystal. At White turn end the Hi collects it, and the practice strip resets to zero.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: An attack kill. Back to zero. A crystal does not do that.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A kill is an enemy removed by an attack.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A payday still fills your bank. It does not reset the quiet count.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ending A finishes with no attack kill, even though it collects one crystal.
directions: [card: ENDING A · no kill · no crystals] [card: ENDING B · no kill · one crystal] [board: the strip stays at nine. Nothing moves.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ending B removes an enemy by attack. Another enemy remains on the board.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The strip is at nine. Which ending draws?

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Choose a card, or watch both and see.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ending A was quiet, so it added one. The tenth space filled.
directions: [sfx: clock settle] [board: the tenth space fills. Every piece stops where it stands. The arrow to the next turn greys out and stays grey.]
[card: QUIET BULLETIN · ten of ten · outlook: finished]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ten quiet turns is a draw. Nobody wins and nobody loses.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Black's turn never starts. That is the Quiet Ten.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ending B killed an enemy by attack. That reset the count, and this turn ends at zero.
directions: [sfx: crystal clink] [board: back to nine. Ending B: one crystal drops into the bank and all ten spaces sweep empty in one pass.]

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: So a busy payday can still be a quiet turn.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: One attack removes an enemy. The strip goes back to zero the moment that piece leaves.
directions: [card: EVIDENCE · proves: what resets this clock and what does not · not checked: what either player will choose to do]
[card: ending A, but one attack removes an enemy piece]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Unless that was their last piece. Then White has already won, and the clock never gets asked.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: I counted the clock. I did not count Black.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Filed. Overruled by the Quiet Ten.
directions: [card: MINI GAME · two separate positions, each starting at quiet nine · no attack kills · a Muju ends on zero reserve, then on one reserve · all other friendly units collect zero · compare the endings]
[board: Pip drops the trumpet card into the drawer marked PIP'S AMENDMENTS (PENDING).]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Attack kill. Back to zero. A crystal does not do that.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The tenth quiet turn ends in a draw after mining, before the next turn starts. Even a piece waiting on the enemy home cannot override it. Ten player turns means five complete rounds. The warning turns amber at seven.

supplement.title: Quiet 10 ends the game before the next turn
supplement.body:
Mine → update quiet count → draw at 10.
The next home check never happens after a draw.
10 player turns = 5 full rounds. Warning at 7.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Nobody needs to answer quickly. This clock counts game turns, not your thinking time.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: That is enough for today if you want.

question: The strip is at nine. Which ending draws?
